programmes.name_en: Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF)
programmes.funder: Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture
programmes.amount_note: INR 1 lakh crore financing facility. 3% per annum interest subvention on loans up to INR 2 crore per project for a maximum of seven years, plus credit guarantee cover under CGTMSE for loans up to INR 2 crore. Eligible beneficiaries may hold up to 25 projects at separate locations.
programmes.deadline_note: Open on a rolling basis; the scheme period was extended and the eligible activity list broadened in 2024.

procedure_steps.detail: Register and file the project on the AIF portal (agriinfra.dac.gov.in).
The application is routed to the chosen lending institution.
Bank sanctions the loan; interest subvention and credit guarantee are applied.
Disbursement against project milestones.

eligibility.other_note: Farmers, FPOs, PACS, marketing cooperative societies, SHGs, joint liability groups, agri-entrepreneurs, startups, agri-tech players and central or state agency-sponsored PPP projects. The project must be post-harvest management infrastructure or a community farming asset. DPIIT recognition is not required.

programmes.name_en: Atal Community Innovation Centre (ACIC)
programmes.funder: Atal Innovation Mission (AIM), NITI Aayog
programmes.amount_note: Grant-in-aid of up to INR 2.5 crore to a host institution to run a community innovation centre in underserved and unserved regions, with the host contributing a matching share.
programmes.deadline_note: The ACIC application window is not currently open; earlier rounds have been completed and results published.
programmes.reopen_note: AIM 2.0 was approved with INR 2,750 crore until March 2028; further ACIC rounds may be announced within that period. Monitor aim.gov.in.

eligibility.other_note: Applicants are host institutions in tier 2/3 cities, aspirational districts, the North East, Jammu and Kashmir and similar underserved regions. Matching contribution required.

programmes.name_en: Atal Incubation Centre (AIC)
programmes.funder: Atal Innovation Mission (AIM), NITI Aayog
programmes.amount_note: Grant-in-aid of up to INR 10 crore over five years to establish and run an incubator. This funds the incubator; startups receive incubation support rather than a direct AIM grant.
programmes.deadline_note: AIM's application portal for new Atal Incubation Centres is not currently accepting fresh applications; the AIC page publishes shortlisted applicants from earlier phases.
programmes.reopen_note: The Union Cabinet approved continuation of the Atal Innovation Mission (AIM 2.0) with a budget of INR 2,750 crore until March 2028, so further calls are expected within that period. Watch aim.gov.in.

eligibility.other_note: Applicants are host institutions (academic, corporate, not-for-profit) proposing to run an incubator, not individual startups. Startups engage with an existing AIC directly.

programmes.source_snippet: The shortlisted applicants for Atal Incubation Centres - Phase 1 are out now!

programmes.name_en: Atal New India Challenge (ANIC)
programmes.funder: Atal Innovation Mission (AIM), NITI Aayog
programmes.amount_note: Grant-in-aid of up to INR 1 crore per selected innovation, plus mentoring and market access, awarded against published national problem statements from partner ministries.
programmes.deadline_note: No ANIC round is currently accepting applications; ANIC 1.0 and 2.0 have concluded.
programmes.reopen_note: ANIC has historically been run as periodic themed editions. AIM 2.0 continues until March 2028, so further editions are plausible; monitor aim.gov.in.

eligibility.other_note: Indian startups and MSMEs with a working prototype addressing a published ANIC problem statement.

programmes.name_en: Atal Tinkering Lab (ATL)
programmes.funder: Atal Innovation Mission (AIM), NITI Aayog
programmes.amount_note: Grant-in-aid of INR 20 lakh over five years to a school to set up and operate a tinkering lab (INR 10 lakh capital and INR 10 lakh operational).
programmes.deadline_note: The ATL application portal is not currently open for new school applications.
programmes.reopen_note: Under AIM 2.0 the government announced an intent to establish a further 10,000 Atal Tinkering Labs; new application windows are expected before March 2028. Monitor aim.gov.in.

eligibility.other_note: Applicants are schools (government, government-aided or private) teaching class VI upwards with the required space. Not a startup funding line, but a common pipeline for student innovators.

programmes.name_local: Startup AP - Andhra Pradesh Innovation Society support
programmes.name_en: Startup AP - Andhra Pradesh Innovation Society support
programmes.funder: Andhra Pradesh Innovation Society (APIS), Government of Andhra Pradesh
programmes.amount_note: Grant, incubation and challenge-based support to Andhra Pradesh startups through APIS, including sector innovation challenges and access to state incubators. Award amounts are set per programme.
programmes.deadline_note: Support runs through periodic challenges and cohort calls announced on apis.ap.gov.in.

eligibility.other_note: DPIIT recognition is a prerequisite. Startups registered or operating in Andhra Pradesh.

programmes.name_local: Andhra Pradesh Innovation and Startup Policy incentives
programmes.name_en: Andhra Pradesh Innovation and Startup Policy incentives
programmes.funder: Information Technology, Electronics and Communications Department, Government of Andhra Pradesh
programmes.amount_note: Startup grant up to INR 15 lakh in phases (upfront initial grant up to INR 2 lakh); up to INR 20 lakh for startups with a Woman/BC/SC/ST/Minority/Differently Abled founder. Under AP Innovation & Startup Policy 4.0 (2024-2029).

eligibility.other_note: DPIIT recognition is a prerequisite. Startup must be registered and operating in Andhra Pradesh.

programmes.source_snippet: Grant up to 15 Lakhs for startups, in a phase wise manner ... Grant up to 20 Lakhs for startup with a founder from Women/BC/SC/ST/Minority/Differently Abled & Others.

programmes.name_local: Assam Startup - The Nest incubation and seed support
programmes.name_en: Assam Startup - The Nest incubation and seed support
programmes.funder: Industries and Commerce Department, Government of Assam (Assam Startup - The Nest)
programmes.amount_note: Incubation at The Nest in Guwahati plus seed support and a monthly sustenance allowance under the Assam Startup Policy. Ceilings are set in the policy notification; the state has also announced a venture fund for Assam startups.
programmes.deadline_note: The Nest runs periodic incubation cohorts; seed support applications follow cohort selection.

procedure_steps.detail: Apply to an Assam Startup - The Nest cohort call.
Screening and pitching before the selection panel.
Incubation at The Nest with a sustenance allowance.
Seed support disbursed against milestones.

eligibility.other_note: Startups founded by Assam residents or registered in Assam. DPIIT recognition is not strictly required for The Nest but is required for several linked state incentives.

programmes.name_local: ASPIRE - A Scheme for Promotion of Innovation, Rural Industries and Entrepreneurship
programmes.name_en: ASPIRE - A Scheme for Promotion of Innovation, Rural Industries and Entrepreneurship
programmes.funder: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME), Government of India
programmes.amount_note: Grant support to set up Livelihood Business Incubators and Technology Business Incubators in rural and agro-based sectors: up to INR 1 crore for a new LBI and up to INR 50 lakh for strengthening an existing one. The incubator, not the entrepreneur, is the grantee.
programmes.deadline_note: Host institution applications are received on the ASPIRE portal; confirm the current window with the Ministry, as the scheme has been folded into consolidated MSME programming.

eligibility.other_note: Applicants are host institutions (KVIC, NSIC, Coir Board, academic institutions, PSUs, private bodies) setting up rural livelihood or technology business incubators. Rural entrepreneurs benefit through the incubator.

programmes.name_en: Atal Innovation Mission (Atal Incubation Centres, Atal Community Innovation Centres, Atal Tinkering Labs)
programmes.funder: Atal Innovation Mission (AIM), NITI Aayog, Government of India
programmes.amount_note: AIM funds institutions (incubators, community innovation centres, school tinkering labs) rather than making direct grants to individual startups; startups benefit indirectly through the 72 Atal Incubation Centres. Per-centre grant ceilings are set in each Expression of Interest. No amount is published on the AIM homepage and the programme pages were not reachable at the time of verification, so amounts are recorded as null.
programmes.deadline_note: As of 14 August 2026 the AIM website states: 'Dear Applicants, please note that the application portal for ATL, AIC and ACIC are not currently open.' AIM runs periodic Expression of Interest calls; no open call was listed at the time of verification.

procedure_steps.detail: Monitor aim.gov.in for the next Expression of Interest for AIC / ACIC / ATL.
Institutions apply through the AIM application portal when a call opens.
Individual startups seeking support should instead approach an existing Atal Incubation Centre directly.

documents_required.doc: Expression of Interest as per the AIM call format
documents_required.note: For host institutions, not individual startups

documents_required.doc: Proof of legal entity status and infrastructure availability

eligibility.other_note: AIM's direct beneficiaries are host institutions (universities, institutions, corporates, NGOs) that set up Atal Incubation Centres, Atal Community Innovation Centres or Atal Tinkering Labs. Startups access support through the 72 operating AICs, which report 3,500+ startups supported and 32,000+ jobs created. DPIIT recognition is not a stated prerequisite, though individual AICs may require it for onward central schemes such as SISFS.

programmes.source_snippet: Dear Applicants, please note that the application portal for ATL, AIC and ACIC are not currently open.

programmes.name_en: BIRAC Biotechnology Ignition Grant (BIG)
programmes.funder: Biotechnology Industry Research Assistance Council (BIRAC), a PSE of the Department of Biotechnology (DBT), Government of India
programmes.amount_note: Up to INR 50 Lakhs as grant-in-aid per BIG Innovator, for a research project with commercialization potential of up to 18 months duration, to take an innovative idea to Proof of Concept.
programmes.deadline_note: The call for proposal is announced twice a year, i.e. on 1st January and 1st July. Call for proposals typically remains open for about 45 days.

procedure_steps.detail: Register on the BIRAC portal following the BIG registration guidelines.
Read the BIG scheme guidelines (revised November 2025) and prepare the proposal in the prescribed proforma.
Submit the proposal online during an open call window (opens 1 January or 1 July, ~45 days).
Shortlisted applicants are evaluated and, if selected, are mentored and monitored through one of the 8 BIG Partner institutions.

documents_required.doc: BIG proposal in the prescribed proforma
Budget breakdown for up to 18 months

documents_required.note: Individual innovators may also apply; a company is required at award stage

eligibility.other_note: Aimed at young startups and individual researchers/innovators in biotechnology and life sciences. Administered through 8 BIG Partners (C-CAMP, KIIT-TBI, IKP, Venture Center, FITT IIT Delhi, SIIC IIT Kanpur, a-IDEA NAARM, SINE IIT Bombay) plus 11 associate partners. DPIIT recognition is not stated as a prerequisite for BIG on the official page.

programmes.source_snippet: BIG provides early-stage funding support of INR 50 Lakhs as grant-in-aid for a period of 18 months to translate their innovative ideas into Proof of Concept. ... The call for proposal is announced twice a year, i.e. on 1st January and 1st July. Call for proposals typically remains open for about 45 days.
programmes.reopen_note: Next call due 1 January 2027 per the page's stated twice-yearly schedule (1 Jan and 1 Jul); window stays open about 45 days.

programmes.name_local: BIRAC Bio-incubators Nurturing Entrepreneurship for Scaling Technologies (BioNEST)
programmes.name_en: BIRAC Bio-incubators Nurturing Entrepreneurship for Scaling Technologies (BioNEST)
programmes.funder: Biotechnology Industry Research Assistance Council (BIRAC), Department of Biotechnology
programmes.amount_note: BIRAC funds the bio-incubator, not the startup. Startups get subsidised wet-lab and analytical infrastructure, mentoring and regulatory support at BioNEST incubators across India.
programmes.deadline_note: Startups apply directly to an individual BioNEST bio-incubator, which runs its own intake. BIRAC calls to set up new BioNEST incubators are periodic.

eligibility.other_note: Startups in life sciences and biotechnology needing shared lab infrastructure. Terms are set by each host incubator.

programmes.name_en: Biotechnology Industry Partnership Programme (BIPP)
programmes.funder: Biotechnology Industry Research Assistance Council (BIRAC), Department of Biotechnology
programmes.amount_note: Cost-shared, milestone-linked support (advance or soft loan plus grant components) for high-risk, future-technology biotech R&D by Indian companies. Amount is proposal-specific.
programmes.deadline_note: Issued through BIRAC calls for proposals.

eligibility.other_note: Indian biotech companies with at least 51% Indian shareholding; significant applicant cost-share required.

programmes.name_local: BIRAC Launching Entrepreneurial driven Affordable Products (LEAP)
programmes.name_en: BIRAC Launching Entrepreneurial driven Affordable Products (LEAP)
programmes.funder: Biotechnology Industry Research Assistance Council (BIRAC), Department of Biotechnology
programmes.amount_note: Support of the order of INR 1 crore for Indian biotech startups to take a validated technology towards global market entry, typically via international partnerships and soft-landing programmes.
programmes.deadline_note: Run through periodic BIRAC calls; check the Call for Proposals page.

eligibility.other_note: Indian biotech companies with at least 51% Indian shareholding and a technology at or beyond proof of concept.

programmes.name_local: BIRAC Promoting Academic Research Conversion to Enterprise (PACE)
programmes.name_en: BIRAC Promoting Academic Research Conversion to Enterprise (PACE)
programmes.funder: Biotechnology Industry Research Assistance Council (BIRAC), Department of Biotechnology
programmes.amount_note: Academic Innovation Research (AIR): project cost up to INR 50 lakh. Contract Research Scheme (CRS): no ceiling on funding.
programmes.deadline_note: Three calls a year per BIRAC: 15 Feb-31 Mar, 15 Jun-31 Jul, 15 Oct-30 Nov.

eligibility.other_note: Primary applicant is an academic institution, university, NGO or research foundation (with government registration/accreditation); industry/LLP partner optional for AIR, mandatory for CRS, with at least 51% Indian-citizen shareholding. DPIIT recognition is not mandatory.

programmes.source_snippet: There are three call for proposals in a year. 15th February – 31st March; 15th June – 31st July; 15th October – 30th November

programmes.name_en: BIRAC SEED Fund (Sustainable Entrepreneurship And Enterprise Development)
programmes.funder: Biotechnology Industry Research Assistance Council (BIRAC), Department of Biotechnology (DBT), Government of India
programmes.amount_note: First equity exposure of up to INR 30 lakhs per post-Proof-of-Concept startup. The money is deployed by selected BioNEST incubators, which receive grant-in-aid of INR 200 lakhs per cycle from BIRAC to invest in biotech startups. Positioned as a bridge between promoter's investment and Angel/Venture investment.
programmes.deadline_note: Startups avail SEED Fund through one of the 16 listed BIRAC SEED Fund Partner incubators; each partner runs its own intake. No central call schedule is published on the BIRAC SEED Fund page.

procedure_steps.detail: Read the BIRAC Incubator SEED Fund guidelines.
Identify and approach one of BIRAC's SEED Fund Partner BioNEST incubators (e.g. C-CAMP, IKP, Venture Center, SINE IIT Bombay, KIIT-TBI, riidl, FITT, VIT-TBI).
Apply to that incubator; the incubator conducts due diligence and makes the equity investment decision.

documents_required.doc: Evidence of completed Proof of Concept
Certificate of Incorporation and cap table

eligibility.other_note: For post-PoC biotech / life sciences startups. Investment is made by the partner BioNEST incubator, not by BIRAC directly, and takes equity. DPIIT recognition is not stated as a prerequisite on the official SEED Fund page.

programmes.source_snippet: SEED Fund is meant for post PoC Startups. It helps Biotech Startups to cover the first Valley of Death enabling Angel investment readiness. ... equity exposure of up to INR 30 lakhs

programmes.name_local: BIRAC Social Innovation programme for Products: Affordable and Relevant to Societal Health (SPARSH)
programmes.name_en: BIRAC Social Innovation programme for Products: Affordable and Relevant to Societal Health (SPARSH)
programmes.funder: Biotechnology Industry Research Assistance Council (BIRAC), Department of Biotechnology
programmes.amount_note: Grant-in-aid of the order of INR 50 lakh over about 18 months to social innovators developing affordable healthcare products for underserved populations, issued against thematic challenge calls.
programmes.deadline_note: Issued as thematic challenge calls; check the BIRAC Call for Proposals page for the live theme and window.

eligibility.other_note: Companies, start-ups and LLPs with minimum 51% Indian ownership may apply alone or in collaboration; academic institutes, universities, NGOs or research foundations (government-registered/accredited) may apply with one or more partners, at least one being a company. Affordable social-health biotech innovations.

programmes.source_snippet: Companies/Start-ups/Limited Liability Partnerships - LLP (with minimum 51% Indian ownership) are eligible to apply either alone, or in collaboration with another Company/Academic Institution

programmes.name_local: Beyond Bengaluru cluster support (Mysuru, Hubballi-Dharwad, Mangaluru, Kalaburagi)
programmes.name_en: Beyond Bengaluru cluster support (Mysuru, Hubballi-Dharwad, Mangaluru, Kalaburagi)
programmes.funder: Karnataka Innovation and Technology Society (KITS), Government of Karnataka
programmes.amount_note: Subsidised incubation, plug-and-play space, and a dedicated ELEVATE Aspire grant track for startups located outside Bengaluru. The Aspire track carries the same INR 50 lakh ELEVATE ceiling.

eligibility.other_note: Startups operating from Karnataka clusters outside Bengaluru. Grant funding is accessed through the ELEVATE Aspire track when the annual ELEVATE call is live.

programmes.name_en: Bihar Startup Policy seed funding
programmes.funder: Department of Industries, Government of Bihar (Startup Bihar)
programmes.amount_note: Seed funding up to INR 10 lakh per startup as an interest-free loan for 10 years (Bihar Startup Policy).
programmes.deadline_note: Applications are accepted on a rolling basis via the Startup Bihar portal.

procedure_steps.detail: Register the startup on the Startup Bihar portal.
Submit the business plan for evaluation.
Screening and presentation before the Startup Bihar selection committee.
Interest-free loan sanctioned and disbursed in tranches.

documents_required.doc: Bihar domicile or address proof of founders

eligibility.other_note: Startup must be registered in Bihar or founders must hold Bihar domicile, and be recognised under the Bihar Startup Policy. DPIIT recognition is not strictly required for the state seed loan but is commonly held.

programmes.source_snippet: Seed Grant upto Rs 10 Lakhs per start-up as interest free loan for 10 years shall be provided to startups.

programmes.name_local: 36Inc - Startup Chhattisgarh incubation and grant support
programmes.name_en: 36Inc - Startup Chhattisgarh incubation and grant support
programmes.funder: Chhattisgarh Infotech Promotion Society (CHiPS), Government of Chhattisgarh
programmes.amount_note: Cohort-based incubation at 36Inc in Naya Raipur with grant support, mentoring and market access for Chhattisgarh startups. Amounts are set per cohort and under the Chhattisgarh startup policy.
programmes.deadline_note: 36Inc runs periodic incubation cohorts; check 36inc.in for the live call.

eligibility.other_note: Startups registered in Chhattisgarh or founded by Chhattisgarh residents. DPIIT recognition is required for several linked state incentives.

programmes.name_local: Chhattisgarh startup policy incentives (interest subsidy and patent reimbursement)
programmes.name_en: Chhattisgarh startup policy incentives (interest subsidy and patent reimbursement)
programmes.funder: Chhattisgarh Infotech Promotion Society (CHiPS), Government of Chhattisgarh
programmes.amount_note: Grant up to INR 10 lakh for startups with a validated PoC to develop an MVP; other incentives under the Chhattisgarh Innovation and Startup Promotion Policy 2025-2030.

eligibility.other_note: DPIIT recognition is a prerequisite. Startup must be registered and operating in Chhattisgarh.

programmes.source_snippet: A grant of up to ₹10 lakhs is available for startups with a validated Proof of Concept (PoC) to develop Minimum Viable Product (MVP).

programmes.name_en: Credit Guarantee Scheme for Startups (CGSS)
programmes.funder: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT); National Credit Guarantee Trustee Company (NCGTC)
programmes.amount_note: Guarantee cover for loans to DPIIT-recognised startups, with a ceiling of INR 20 crore of guarantee per borrower (raised from INR 10 crore in 2025). Cover is 80% of the amount in default for loans up to INR 3 crore, 75% for loans above INR 3 crore up to INR 5 crore, and 85% for startups in 27 identified champion sectors.

procedure_steps.detail: Approach a Member Institution (scheduled bank, NBFC or AIF registered with NCGTC).
Lender appraises the credit facility and applies for guarantee cover on the NCGTC portal.
Guarantee fee is paid annually on the outstanding amount.

eligibility.other_note: DPIIT recognition is a prerequisite. Startup must be at a stage generating stable revenue as assessed by audited monthly statements over a 12-month period, or otherwise creditworthy per the lender. Must not be in default to any lending or investing institution and not classified as NPA.

programmes.source_snippet: The CGSS offers collateral-free credit guarantees for DPIIT-recognized startups ... Maximum guarantee cover per borrower upto Rs.20 crore.

programmes.name_local: Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises (CGTMSE)
programmes.name_en: Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises (CGTMSE)
programmes.funder: CGTMSE (Ministry of MSME and SIDBI)
programmes.amount_note: Guarantee cover for collateral-free credit to micro and small enterprises, with the guarantee ceiling raised to INR 10 crore. Cover ranges from 75% to 85% of the amount in default depending on borrower category, with higher cover for women, SC/ST, North East and micro loans up to INR 5 lakh.

procedure_steps.detail: Approach a CGTMSE Member Lending Institution (bank, NBFC, small finance bank or RRB) for a credit facility.
Lender appraises and sanctions the facility without collateral or third-party guarantee.
Lender lodges the guarantee application on the CGTMSE portal and pays the annual guarantee fee.

eligibility.other_note: Micro and small enterprises registered on Udyam, in manufacturing or services (retail trade is covered under specified conditions). New and existing enterprises are eligible. DPIIT recognition is not required - startups seeking a startup-specific guarantee should use CGSS instead.

programmes.source_snippet: Fund and non-fund based (Letters of Credit, Bank Guarantee etc.) credit facilities up to ₹10 crore per eligible borrower are covered under the guarantee scheme

programmes.name_en: CGTMSE Credit Guarantee Scheme for Micro and Small Enterprises
programmes.funder: Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises (CGTMSE), set up by the Ministry of MSME, Government of India and SIDBI
programmes.amount_note: CGTMSE does not lend. It guarantees collateral-free credit extended by Member Lending Institutions to Micro and Small Enterprises. The guarantee ceiling has been increased to Rs. 10 crore (raised from Rs. 500 lakh). The guarantee coverage percentage and the annual guarantee fee slabs are set out in CGTMSE circulars which I could not load at the time of verification, so they are recorded as null rather than guessed; the homepage does state that the annual guarantee fee structure was revised and reduced for guarantees above Rs 1 crore.
programmes.deadline_note: Continuously available. Guarantee cover is applied for by the lending bank, not by the borrower.

procedure_steps.detail: Approach a CGTMSE Member Lending Institution (a bank, RRB or eligible financial institution) for a collateral-free credit facility.
The lender appraises the proposal and, on sanction, lodges the application for guarantee cover with CGTMSE.
CGTMSE issues the guarantee; the borrower pays the applicable annual guarantee fee through the lender.

documents_required.doc: Project report and financial projections for the lender's appraisal
KYC and constitution documents of the enterprise

eligibility.other_note: Eligible borrowers are Micro & Small Enterprises (MSEs). Enhanced terms apply for women entrepreneurs, transgender entrepreneurs, SC/ST entrepreneurs, persons with disability (PwD), ZED certified units, informal micro enterprises (IME) and units in Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh. DPIIT recognition is NOT required for CGTMSE; MSME/Udyam registration is the relevant credential. A separate Credit Guarantee Scheme for Startups (CGSS) exists for DPIIT-recognised startups and is administered by NCGTC, not CGTMSE.

programmes.source_snippet: Ceiling of guarantee coverage increased to ₹10 crore

programmes.name_local: Delhi Startup Policy 2022 - interest-free loan and support
programmes.name_en: Delhi Startup Policy 2022 - interest-free loan and support
programmes.funder: Department of Industries, Government of the National Capital Territory of Delhi
programmes.amount_note: Interest-free loan of up to INR 20 lakh reported under the Delhi Startup Policy 2022, plus a monthly stipend to founders for up to one year and reimbursement of legal, patent and consultancy costs.
programmes.deadline_note: The Delhi Startup Policy was approved in 2022 and the implementing mechanism has been rolled out in phases. Confirm the current application window and the operative loan ceiling with the Department of Industries before relying on it.

eligibility.other_note: DPIIT recognition is a prerequisite. Startup must be registered in Delhi. Selection is made by a Startup Policy Monitoring Committee.

programmes.name_en: DPIIT Startup Recognition (gateway to Startup India benefits, incl. Section 56 angel tax exemption)
programmes.funder: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India
programmes.amount_note: Recognition carries no cash award. It is the gateway credential: self-certification under labour and environment laws, IPR fast-tracking, public procurement relaxations, and eligibility to then apply for 80-IAC income tax exemption and for exemption under Section 56 of the Income Tax Act (angel tax). Almost every Indian central startup scheme requires it.
programmes.deadline_note: Applications accepted at any time on the National Single Window System. No fee is charged.

procedure_steps.detail: Create an account on the National Single Window System (nsws.gov.in) and add the form 'Registration as a Startup'.
Submit entity details and supporting documents; recognition is granted against the definition in G.S.R. notification 108(E).
After receiving the DPIIT Certificate, apply separately for 80-IAC tax exemption and for Section 56 (angel tax) exemption.

documents_required.doc: Brief write-up on innovation and scalability

eligibility.other_note: Must be incorporated as a Private Limited Company or registered as a Partnership Firm, Limited Liability Partnership, or Cooperative Society. Turnover less than INR 200 Crores (INR 300 Crores for DeepTech startups) in any of the previous financial years. Startup status lasts up to 10 years (20 years for DeepTech) from incorporation. An entity formed by splitting up or reconstruction of an existing business is not a Startup. On angel tax: the official page still signposts an application route for 'Exemption under Section 56 of the Income Tax Act (Angel Tax)'. I did not independently verify the current statutory position of Section 56(2)(viib) on an Income Tax Department page, so the live status of that exemption route is unconfirmed here.

programmes.source_snippet: Turnover should be less than INR 200 Crores (INR 300 Crores for DeepTech startups) in any of the previous financial years. An entity shall be considered a startup for up to 10 years (20 years for DeepTech startups)

programmes.name_en: DRDO Technology Development Fund (TDF)
programmes.funder: Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO), Ministry of Defence
programmes.amount_note: Up to INR 50 crore per project (ceiling raised from INR 10 crore in 2022) covering up to 90% of the development cost of defence technologies by Indian MSMEs and startups.
programmes.deadline_note: DRDO publishes technology development problem statements on the TDF portal; each statement carries its own submission window.

eligibility.other_note: Indian MSMEs and startups with an Indian development partner; the project must map to a published DRDO problem statement. DPIIT recognition is not mandatory but is commonly held by applicants.

programmes.source_snippet: Technology Development Fund Scheme is a flagship program of MoD executed by DRDO ... Funding of up to Rs. 50 Cr. per project is provided to the industry as Grant-in-Aid.

programmes.name_en: Fund of Funds for Startups (FFS)
programmes.funder: Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI) for DPIIT
programmes.amount_note: INR 10,000 crore corpus committed to SEBI-registered Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs), which in turn invest in startups. SIDBI contributes up to 15% of an AIF corpus (up to 20% for certain funds). Startups do not apply directly; they raise from the participating AIFs.
programmes.deadline_note: AIFs (daughter funds) may approach SIDBI on a rolling basis. Startups access the money by raising from an FFS-backed AIF.

eligibility.other_note: Startups are not direct applicants. The AIF must invest at least twice the SIDBI commitment into DPIIT-recognised startups. DPIIT recognition is a prerequisite.

programmes.name_local: Startup India Fund of Funds for Startups 2.0 (FFS 2.0)
programmes.name_en: Startup India Fund of Funds for Startups 2.0 (FFS 2.0)
programmes.funder: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), implemented by SIDBI
programmes.amount_note: Corpus INR 10,000 crore for commitments to eligible AIFs, which invest in startups (not direct grants to startups).
programmes.deadline_note: Operational guidelines issued 25 April 2026. AIF managers apply to the Implementation Agency on a rolling basis; two-stage selection with screening by SIDBI followed by a Venture Capital Investment Committee.

procedure_steps.detail: AIF manager applies to SIDBI as Implementation Agency.
Initial screening by the Implementation Agency.
Evaluation by the Venture Capital Investment Committee on team track record, fund management capability and investment strategy.
Capital commitment and drawdown; the AIF then invests in DPIIT-recognised startups.

eligibility.other_note: Applicants to FFS 2.0 are SEBI-registered AIFs. Downstream investee startups must be DPIIT-recognised.

programmes.source_snippet: The Government has notified the Startup India Fund of Funds 2.0 (Startup India FoF 2.0) with a total corpus of ₹10,000 crore for the purpose of mobilizing venture and growth capital for the startup ecosystem of the country.

programmes.name_en: Goa Startup Policy incentives
programmes.funder: Startup and IT Promotion Cell, Government of Goa
programmes.amount_note: Under the Goa Startup Policy: a monthly sustenance stipend for founders, reimbursement of incubation and co-working costs, patent cost reimbursement, and a grant linked to reaching defined milestones. Ceilings are set in the policy notification.
programmes.deadline_note: Applications are made on a rolling basis after obtaining Goa Startup Certification.

procedure_steps.detail: Apply for Goa Startup Certification on startup.goa.gov.in.
On certification, apply for individual incentives.
Verification by the Startup Promotion Cell.
Disbursement or reimbursement.

eligibility.other_note: Startup must be registered in Goa and hold Goa Startup Certification. DPIIT recognition is accepted as supporting evidence and is a prerequisite for some linked central benefits.

programmes.name_local: i-Hub Gujarat startup and student innovation support
programmes.name_en: i-Hub Gujarat startup and student innovation support
programmes.funder: i-Hub (Gujarat Student Startup and Innovation Hub), Government of Gujarat
programmes.amount_note: Startup Srujan Seed Support (S4) grants of INR 2.5 lakh to 10 lakh.
programmes.deadline_note: Cohorts are announced periodically on ihubgujarat.in.

eligibility.other_note: Student innovators and early-stage startups from Gujarat institutions. DPIIT recognition is not required for i-Hub cohorts.

programmes.source_snippet: Startup Srujan Seed Support Grant (S4) (INR 2.5-10 Lacs). Any Innovator/Startup up to the age of 35 years

programmes.name_local: Gujarat Scheme for Assistance to Startups and Innovation (Industries Department)
programmes.name_en: Gujarat Scheme for Assistance to Startups and Innovation (Industries Department)
programmes.funder: Industries Commissionerate, Government of Gujarat
programmes.amount_note: Under the Gujarat industrial policy startup scheme: a monthly sustenance allowance for up to one year (with a higher rate for women founders), assistance for product development, and support for marketing, publicity and acceleration. Exact ceilings are set in the current Government Resolution - reported product development assistance is of the order of INR 30 lakh.
programmes.deadline_note: Applications are made on a rolling basis through a nodal institution approved by the Industries Commissionerate.

eligibility.other_note: Startup must be recommended by an approved nodal institution in Gujarat and be working on an innovative product or process, with Gujarat operations. DPIIT recognition is not strictly required but is commonly held.

programmes.source_snippet: Assistance up to INR 30 lakh as a seed support to the startups. Sustenance allowance of INR 20,000 per month to the startups and INR 25,000 per month to women

programmes.name_en: Student Startup and Innovation Policy 2.0 (SSIP 2.0)
programmes.funder: Education Department, Government of Gujarat
programmes.amount_note: Start-up Srujan Seed Support up to INR 10 lakh under SSIP 2.0.
programmes.deadline_note: Students apply through their institution's SSIP cell on a rolling basis; institutional grant proposals are submitted via the SSIP portal.

procedure_steps.detail: Register as a student innovator on ssipgujarat.in via your institution.
Submit the idea or prototype proposal in the prescribed grant proposal format.
Institute-level SSIP committee evaluation.
Grant disbursed by the institution against milestones.

eligibility.other_note: Any individual or group of individuals with an innovative idea or concept is eligible; the applicant is normally a student of a Gujarat institution. Universities, education institutions, incubation centres, PSUs, R&D institutions and private establishments are eligible as supporting institutions. Incorporation and DPIIT recognition are NOT required.

programmes.source_snippet: Support to 500 Start-up under Start-up Srujan Seed Support (Up to INR 10 Lac).

programmes.name_local: Himachal Pradesh Startup, Innovation Projects and New Industries Scheme
programmes.name_en: Himachal Pradesh Startup, Innovation Projects and New Industries Scheme
programmes.funder: Department of Industries, Government of Himachal Pradesh
programmes.amount_note: Seed fund up to INR 50 lakh (HIMSUP Yojana); sustenance allowance INR 25,000 per month for one year; 5% interest subvention on loans up to INR 25 lakh.
programmes.deadline_note: Applications are made through state-recognised incubators on a rolling basis.

eligibility.other_note: Startup must be incubated at a Himachal Pradesh government-recognised incubator, with operations in the state. DPIIT recognition is generally expected.

programmes.source_snippet: Seed Fund Upto INR 50 Lakhs (Under HIMSUP Yoiana). Interest subvention @ 5% up to a loan of Rs. 25 lakh for three

programmes.name_local: Haryana Startup Policy seed grant and incentives
programmes.name_en: Haryana Startup Policy seed grant and incentives
programmes.funder: Department of Industries and Commerce, Government of Haryana (Startup Haryana)
programmes.amount_note: Under the Haryana State Startup Policy: a seed grant to recognised startups, reimbursement of lease rental at approved incubators, reimbursement of patent and IPR costs (higher for international filings), and marketing assistance. Ceilings are set in the policy notification.
programmes.deadline_note: Rolling applications after obtaining Startup Haryana recognition.

procedure_steps.detail: Register on the Startup Haryana portal.
Apply for the specific incentive with supporting documents.
Scrutiny by the Department of Industries and Commerce.
Sanction and disbursement.

eligibility.other_note: DPIIT recognition is a prerequisite. Startup must be registered and operating in Haryana and recognised on the Startup Haryana portal.

programmes.name_local: T-Works prototyping and hardware fabrication support
programmes.name_en: T-Works prototyping and hardware fabrication support
programmes.funder: T-Works (Government of Telangana)
programmes.amount_note: Access to India's largest prototyping centre - CNC machining, PCB fabrication, injection moulding and electronics labs - at subsidised rates for hardware startups, plus periodic grant-backed prototyping challenges.

eligibility.other_note: Hardware innovators, students and startups. Membership-based access; not restricted to Telangana entities. DPIIT recognition is not required.

programmes.name_local: IndiaAI Mission - Startup Financing and Application Development Initiative
programmes.name_en: IndiaAI Mission - Startup Financing and Application Development Initiative
programmes.funder: IndiaAI Independent Business Division, Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
programmes.amount_note: Funding support for AI startups and application development under the INR 10,372 crore IndiaAI Mission, delivered through themed challenges (IndiaAI Innovation Challenge, foundation models, AI for social impact) plus subsidised access to GPU compute. Award amounts are set per challenge.
programmes.deadline_note: Support is released through periodic IndiaAI challenge calls and expressions of interest; check indiaai.gov.in for live calls.

eligibility.other_note: Indian startups, researchers and institutions working on AI. Specific eligibility, including whether DPIIT recognition is required, varies by challenge.

programmes.name_en: Jharkhand Startup Policy incentives
programmes.funder: Department of Industries, Mines and Geology, Government of Jharkhand
programmes.amount_note: Reimbursement-style incentives: one-time marketing grant max Rs 10 lakh; 50% lease rental up to Rs 5 lakh/yr for 3 yrs; 30% internet and electricity bills up to Rs 60,000/yr each; Rs 5,000/month sustenance stipend for up to 3 members for 12 months; full reimbursement of domestic/international patent filing costs.
programmes.deadline_note: Applications are routed through state-recognised incubators; confirm the currently notified Jharkhand Startup Policy period with the Department of Industries.

eligibility.other_note: Must be registered in Jharkhand, turnover below INR 25 Cr, less than 5 years since incorporation, no more than 50 employees.

programmes.source_snippet: One time marketing grant of maximum Rs. 10 lakh will be provided to Startups ... Startup needs to be registered in Jharkhand, and must have turnover less than INR 25 Cr, and less than 5 years from its incorporation date

programmes.name_local: Jammu and Kashmir Startup Policy incentives
programmes.name_en: Jammu and Kashmir Startup Policy incentives
programmes.funder: Industries and Commerce Department, Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir
programmes.amount_note: One-time seed assistance up to Rs 20 lakh in 4 equal instalments for JKEDI-recognised startups; co-working space at subsidised rates.
programmes.deadline_note: Applications are routed through recognised incubators; confirm the current policy period with the Industries and Commerce Department.

eligibility.other_note: DPIIT recognition is a prerequisite. Startup must be registered and operating in Jammu and Kashmir.

programmes.source_snippet: A one-time assistance of up total 20 lakhs (in 4 equal installments) shall be provided to startups recognized by JKEDI.

programmes.name_en: ELEVATE (Karnataka Grant-in-Aid for Startups)
programmes.funder: Department of Electronics, IT, BT and S&T, Government of Karnataka (Karnataka Innovation and Technology Society)
programmes.amount_note: Grant-in-Aid of up to INR 50 lakh, disbursed in two equal milestone-linked tranches.
programmes.deadline_note: ELEVATE 2026 (25th call) opened 25 May 2026 at 09:00 IST and closed 15 July 2026 at 17:00 IST across four tracks: ELEVATE 2026, ELEVATE Aspire 2026 (Beyond Bengaluru), ELEVATE Unnati 2026 (SC/ST-led) and ELEVATE Shakti 2026 (women-led).
programmes.reopen_note: ELEVATE 2026 microsite (elevate.startupkarnataka.in) shows 'Coming Soon' as of 2026-10-05; no dates published.

procedure_steps.detail: Register on the ELEVATE portal when the call is live and choose a track.
Submit the application with product, team and financial details.
Screening, followed by pitching before an evaluation committee.
Grant sanctioned and released in two equal milestone-linked tranches.

eligibility.other_note: Startup must be within 10 years of incorporation, have turnover not exceeding INR 200 crore in any financial year, be based anywhere in Karnataka, have a minimum team size of two, and must not have been an ELEVATE grant beneficiary in the last 3 years. DPIIT recognition is not a stated prerequisite for ELEVATE, but Startup Karnataka registration is required.

programmes.source_snippet: A one-time grant of up to Rs. 50 Lakhs is given to encourage innovators who may need early-stage funding to develop a prototype, market development and scale-up

programmes.name_en: Idea2PoC (Karnataka Proof of Concept Grant)
programmes.funder: Karnataka Innovation and Technology Society (KITS), Government of Karnataka
programmes.amount_note: Historically up to INR 50 lakh grant-in-aid for taking an idea to proof of concept. Idea2PoC has been folded into the ELEVATE programme, which carries the same ceiling.
programmes.deadline_note: Idea2PoC is no longer run as a separate branded call; it is delivered under the ELEVATE programme.
programmes.reopen_note: ELEVATE 2026 microsite (elevate.startupkarnataka.in) shows 'Coming Soon' as of 2026-10-05; no dates published.

eligibility.other_note: Superseded by ELEVATE. Apply through ELEVATE instead.

programmes.source_snippet: A one-time grant of up to Rs. 50 Lakhs is given to encourage innovators who may need early-stage funding to develop a prototype, market development and scale-up

programmes.name_local: Karnataka Startup Policy incentives (patent, marketing and interest subsidy)
programmes.name_en: Karnataka Startup Policy incentives (patent, marketing and interest subsidy)
programmes.funder: Department of Electronics, IT, BT and S&T, Government of Karnataka
programmes.amount_note: Karnataka Startup Policy 2025-30: patent subsidy up to Rs 15 lakh per year covering domestic and international filings, plus quality-certification reimbursement and other incentives.

eligibility.other_note: Startups registered on the Startup Karnataka portal with operations in Karnataka. Reimbursement claims require proof of expenditure. DPIIT recognition is accepted as supporting evidence and required for some linked central benefits.

programmes.source_snippet: Patent Subsidy: Financial support of up to INR 15 lakhs per year, covering both domestic and international patent filings.

programmes.name_en: ELEVATE / Idea2PoC grant-in-aid, Startup Karnataka
programmes.funder: Karnataka Innovation and Technology Society (KITS) / Karnataka Startup Cell, Department of Electronics, IT, BT and Science & Technology, Government of Karnataka
programmes.amount_note: A one-time, non-dilutive, milestone-linked grant-in-aid to take an idea to proof of concept, run in multiple tracks (general, Aspire for Beyond Bengaluru, Shakti for women-led, Unnati for SC/ST-led). The commonly cited ceiling is INR 50 lakh, but neither startup.karnataka.gov.in nor elevate.startupkarnataka.gov.in would resolve or load at the time of verification, so the amount is recorded as null rather than taken from aggregator sites.
programmes.deadline_note: ELEVATE runs as an annual competitive challenge with multiple tracks, each with its own window. No open window was confirmable from an official Government of Karnataka page at the time of verification.

procedure_steps.detail: Check the current ELEVATE call and track-specific eligibility on the Startup Karnataka portal.
Register and submit the application on the ELEVATE portal during an open window.
Shortlisted startups pitch to an evaluation panel; selected startups receive grant-in-aid released against milestones.

documents_required.doc: Certificate of Incorporation showing a registered office in Karnataka
Proof of concept / prototype plan with milestones and budget

documents_required.note: Track-specific: SC/ST or women shareholding thresholds for Unnati and Shakti

eligibility.other_note: Startup must be registered and headquartered in Karnataka. Track-specific criteria apply for the Aspire (outside Bengaluru Urban), Shakti (women-led) and Unnati (SC/ST-led) tracks. DPIIT recognition is generally expected by Karnataka for state startup benefits but I could not confirm this on an official Karnataka page at the time of verification.

programmes.source_snippet: A one-time grant of up to Rs. 50 Lakhs is given to encourage innovators who may need early-stage funding to develop a prototype, market development and scale-up
programmes.reopen_note: ELEVATE 2026 microsite (elevate.startupkarnataka.in) shows 'Coming Soon' as of 2026-10-05; no dates published.

programmes.name_en: Kerala Startup Mission Idea Grant
programmes.funder: Kerala Startup Mission (KSUM), Government of Kerala
programmes.amount_note: Financial assistance of up to INR 3 lakh for startups at the ideation, design or proof-of-concept stage.
programmes.deadline_note: Applications are accepted on a rolling basis; an applicant cannot reapply within 3 months of a previous application.

procedure_steps.detail: Apply through the KSUM grants portal.
Shortlisting by KSUM.
Pitch before an Expert Committee, evaluated on team, product innovation, marketing, financials and fund utilisation plan.
Approval, document submission and agreement.
Fund disbursement followed by a progress report.

eligibility.other_note: Startups at ideation, designing or PoC stage; innovators based in Kerala; only innovative technology-based products; incorporation (Pvt Ltd/LLP/OPC) and KSUM Unique ID mandatory only before disbursal; reapply after 3 months.

programmes.source_snippet: Under this program, eligible startups can receive financial assistance of up to Rs 3 lakhs.

programmes.name_local: Kerala Startup Mission IP, market access and patent support
programmes.name_en: Kerala Startup Mission IP, market access and patent support
programmes.funder: Kerala Startup Mission (KSUM), Government of Kerala
programmes.amount_note: Reimbursement of patent filing costs (domestic and international), support for participation in international events and trade shows, and subsidised co-working space at KSUM facilities. Ceilings are published per scheme.

eligibility.other_note: DPIIT recognition is a prerequisite. Kerala-registered startup with an active KSUM Unique ID.

programmes.name_local: Kerala Startup Mission Scaleup Seed Fund
programmes.name_en: Kerala Startup Mission Scaleup Seed Fund
programmes.funder: Kerala Startup Mission (KSUM), Government of Kerala
programmes.amount_note: A larger follow-on soft loan for Kerala startups that have demonstrated revenue traction and are scaling. The ceiling and interest terms are published on the KSUM scheme page.

eligibility.other_note: Revenue-stage startups: at least Rs 25 lakh revenue from the product in last four quarters or Rs 25 lakh investment from angel network/VC, and at least Rs 5 lakh revenue in the previous quarter; innovative technology products, not generally service startups or trade/commerce SMEs.

programmes.source_snippet: This is designed to help revenue-stage startups expand and commercialize innovative, technology-based products.

programmes.name_en: Kerala Startup Mission Seed Fund
programmes.funder: Kerala Startup Mission (KSUM), Government of Kerala
programmes.amount_note: Up to INR 15 lakh as a soft loan at 6% simple interest per annum, with a 12-month moratorium followed by 36 monthly instalments. Released in tranches, typically half after document submission and the remainder after a progress report.
programmes.deadline_note: Scheme page shows 'Coming Soon' as of 2026-10-05.

procedure_steps.detail: Apply on the KSUM portal with an active KSUM Unique ID.
Shortlisting around day 15.
Pitching round around day 30.
Agreement and tranche-wise disbursement.
Progress report and expert committee review before the final tranche.

documents_required.doc: Certificate of incorporation as an LLP or Private Limited Company registered in Kerala
MCA status showing Active or Active Compliant

eligibility.other_note: DPIIT recognition is a prerequisite. Must be registered in Kerala as an LLP or Private Limited Company with an active KSUM Unique ID and DIPP registration, MCA status 'Active' or 'Active Compliant', working on an innovative product or technology (service-based startups excluded), with no pending dues to government agencies or KSUM. Director's CIBIL score preferably above 750.

programmes.source_snippet: Under this scheme, early stage startups can receive seed funding (loan) against purchase orders to support product development, customer development, marketing, and scaling up.

programmes.name_en: Chips to Startup (C2S) Programme
programmes.funder: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)
programmes.amount_note: No direct cash grant to startups. Provides access to industry-grade EDA tools, foundry access and MPW shuttle runs, design flows and mentoring for VLSI and system-on-chip design at 100+ participating academic institutions, R&D organisations and startups.
programmes.deadline_note: Participation is granted through periodic MeitY calls for institutions and startups; check the C2S portal for the live call.

eligibility.other_note: Indian academic institutions, R&D organisations and startups working on semiconductor and VLSI design. Designs must be taped out within the programme period.

programmes.name_local: GENESIS - Gen-Next Support for Innovative Startups
programmes.name_en: GENESIS - Gen-Next Support for Innovative Startups
programmes.funder: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)
programmes.amount_note: INR 490 crore scheme over five years. Early-stage support up to INR 10 lakh with no matching-fund requirement; pilot funding averaging INR 40 lakh and up to INR 50 lakh with no matching-fund requirement; deep-tech startups up to a ceiling of INR 1 crore per startup. An investment component requires 1:1 private matching.
programmes.deadline_note: Delivered through roughly 50 implementing agencies, preferably in tier 2 and tier 3 cities, each running its own intake. Check MeitY Startup Hub for live implementing-agency calls.

procedure_steps.detail: Register the startup on MeitY Startup Hub (msh.meity.gov.in).
Apply to a GENESIS implementing agency when its call is live.
Structured expert selection process run by the implementing agency.
Milestone-linked disbursement.

eligibility.other_note: DPIIT recognition is a prerequisite. Shareholding by Indian promoters must be at least 51%. A full-time CEO and a market-ready product are required for certain funding categories. Focus is on startups in tier 2 and tier 3 cities. Registration with MeitY Startup Hub is expected.

programmes.source_snippet: MeitY has envisaged an umbrella scheme GENESIS (Gen-Next Support for Innovative Startups) with a budget of 490 Crores for 5 years to discover, support, grow and accelerate successful startups in Tier-II and Tier-III cities

programmes.name_local: SAMRIDH - Startup Accelerators of MeitY for Product Innovation, Development and Growth
programmes.name_en: SAMRIDH - Startup Accelerators of MeitY for Product Innovation, Development and Growth
programmes.funder: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)
programmes.amount_note: One-to-one matching funding support of up to Rs 40 lakh per startup.
programmes.deadline_note: Applications are made to a MeitY-empanelled SAMRIDH accelerator when it opens a cohort; accelerators run 6-month acceleration programmes each year.

procedure_steps.detail: Register on MeitY Startup Hub.
Apply to an empanelled SAMRIDH accelerator during its open cohort call.
Accelerator due diligence and selection; investment committee approval.
MeitY contribution released alongside the matching investor commitment.

eligibility.other_note: DPIIT recognition is a prerequisite. Startup must have a market-ready product with customer traction, and a matching investment commitment from the accelerator or an investor.

programmes.source_snippet: one-to-one matching funding support of up to ₹40 lakh.

programmes.name_en: MeitY Startup Hub (MSH)
programmes.funder: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)
programmes.amount_note: A national platform, not a grant. Registration on MSH is the gateway to MeitY scheme benefits (GENESIS, SAMRIDH, TIDE 2.0, incubation and challenge programmes) and to MeitY incubator networks.

eligibility.other_note: Open to Indian tech startups, incubators and mentors. Registration on MSH is a practical prerequisite for most MeitY startup funding; DPIIT recognition is required for the funding schemes themselves.

programmes.name_local: TIDE 2.0 - Technology Incubation and Development of Entrepreneurs
programmes.name_en: TIDE 2.0 - Technology Incubation and Development of Entrepreneurs
programmes.funder: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)
programmes.amount_note: Through 51 MeitY-supported incubators: an Entrepreneur-in-Residence grant of up to about INR 4 lakh, and TIDE grants of up to about INR 7 lakh per startup, in ICT-led areas such as IoT, AI, blockchain, robotics and cybersecurity. Amounts are administered by each host incubator.
programmes.deadline_note: Applications go to individual TIDE 2.0 incubators, each running its own cohort intake. Verify with the host incubator whether TIDE 2.0 funds are still available, as the scheme period has been extended more than once.

eligibility.other_note: Indian tech startups working in ICT-led focus areas, incubated at a TIDE 2.0 incubator. DPIIT recognition is generally expected by host incubators.

programmes.source_snippet: TIDE 2.0 will promote tech entrepreneurship through financial and technical support to incubators engaged in supporting ICT startups

programmes.name_local: Maharashtra Grand Challenge and Innovation Challenges
programmes.name_en: Maharashtra Grand Challenge and Innovation Challenges
programmes.funder: Maharashtra State Innovation Society (MSInS)
programmes.amount_note: Current edition (Fisheries Department problem statements): prize up to Rs 5 lakh and pilot up to Rs 15 lakh per problem statement.
programmes.deadline_note: No deadline published on the page.

eligibility.other_note: Open to domestic and foreign individuals, teams, companies, non-profits, academic institutions and government agencies, subject to Indian tax and Maharashtra rules.

programmes.source_snippet: In the current edition Maharashtra State Innovation Society in association with Fisheries Department calling for innovative ideas and solutions to solve problems faced by Fisheries department

programmes.name_local: MSInS startup support (incubation, IPR and quality testing reimbursement)
programmes.name_en: MSInS startup support (incubation, IPR and quality testing reimbursement)
programmes.funder: Maharashtra State Innovation Society (MSInS)
programmes.amount_note: IPR reimbursement: 100% of qualifying invoices (excl. tax) up to Rs 2 lakh for domestic IP and Rs 10 lakh for international IP per startup; post-grant reimbursement.

eligibility.other_note: DPIIT recognition is a prerequisite. Startup must be registered and operating in Maharashtra.

programmes.source_snippet: Maximum INR 2 Lakhs will be supported for domestic IP application (per start-up, covering all forms of IPR). Maximum INR 10 Lakhs will be supported for international IP application

programmes.name_en: Maharashtra Startup Week
programmes.funder: Maharashtra State Innovation Society (MSInS), Skill, Employment, Entrepreneurship and Innovation Department
programmes.amount_note: Winners receive work orders of up to Rs 15 lakh from MSInS to pilot their solutions with state departments.
programmes.deadline_note: Run as an annual flagship edition; applications open for a defined window each year against departmental problem statements. Check msins.in for the current edition.

procedure_steps.detail: Apply on the MSInS portal during the Startup Week call.
Shortlisting and pitching before a jury.
Selected startups are awarded a government work order for a pilot deployment.

eligibility.other_note: DPIIT recognition is a prerequisite. Startup should be registered in Maharashtra or willing to operate there, with a solution mapped to a published government problem statement.

programmes.source_snippet: Winners receive work orders of up to Rs 15 lakh. From the Maharashtra State Innovation Society to pilot their solutions within different state departments.

programmes.name_en: Meghalaya Startup Policy grant support
programmes.funder: Planning Department / Meghalaya Basin Development Authority, Government of Meghalaya
programmes.amount_note: Meghalaya Startup Policy 2018 incentives: State GST reimbursement up to Rs 7 lakh/yr for 7 yrs; power subsidy 50% up to Rs 10 lakh/yr for 5 yrs; patent reimbursement up to Rs 2 lakh domestic / Rs 5 lakh international; lease rental 50% up to Rs 2 lakh/yr; digital upgrade 50% up to Rs 2 lakh.
programmes.deadline_note: Delivered through periodic calls announced on the Meghalaya startup hub portal.

eligibility.other_note: Registered in Meghalaya or employs at least 60% of qualified workforce from Meghalaya; incorporated within last 7 years (10 for biotech); turnover not above INR 25 crore.

programmes.source_snippet: Startups shall be eligible for annual reimbursement of State GST paid in sales of goods for a period of 7 years subject to a maximum of INR 7 lakh per startup per year

programmes.name_local: Madhya Pradesh incubator and Centre of Excellence support
programmes.name_en: Madhya Pradesh incubator and Centre of Excellence support
programmes.funder: Department of MSME and Department of Science and Technology, Government of Madhya Pradesh
programmes.amount_note: Incubator grants: one-time capital grant max 50% or Rs 1 crore (whichever less) for fixed cost; TBI top-up up to Rs 50 lakh; Livelihood Business Incubators in tribal districts up to Rs 100 lakh.

eligibility.other_note: Host institutions apply for incubator support; startups apply to individual incubators.

programmes.source_snippet: One-time capital grant of max. 50% or INR 1 Crore (whichever is less) for Fixed Cost Investment (excluding land& building) for setting up incubator.

programmes.name_local: Startup MP - Madhya Pradesh Startup Policy incentives
programmes.name_en: Startup MP - Madhya Pradesh Startup Policy incentives
programmes.funder: Department of MSME, Government of Madhya Pradesh
programmes.amount_note: MP startup incentives: sustenance allowance Rs 10,000/month up to 1 yr; 50% lease rental up to Rs 5,000/month for 3 yrs; patent assistance up to Rs 5 lakh; 15% of first investment received up to Rs 15 lakh; special grant up to Rs 1 crore (State Innovation Challenge).

procedure_steps.detail: Register the startup on the Startup MP portal.
Apply for the specific incentive with proof of expenditure.
Departmental verification and sanction.
Reimbursement to the startup's bank account.

eligibility.other_note: DPIIT recognition is a prerequisite. Startup must be DPIIT-recognised and registered on the Startup MP portal, with operations in Madhya Pradesh.

programmes.source_snippet: Patent Assistance: Maximum assistance of Rs.5 lakh for obtaining a patent subject to the condition that the patent is obtained for a startup established in the state.

programmes.name_local: MSME Design Scheme (Design Projects and Student Design Projects)
programmes.name_en: MSME Design Scheme (Design Projects and Student Design Projects)
programmes.funder: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME), Government of India
programmes.amount_note: Design project: GoI pays 75% (Micro) / 60% (Small & Medium) of cost up to Rs 40 lakh. Student design project: 75% up to Rs 2.5 lakh.

eligibility.other_note: Udyam-registered MSMEs seeking product or packaging design support, working with a design institute or empanelled designer; student teams apply under the Student Design Project component. DPIIT recognition is not required.

programmes.source_snippet: 75% (Micro) and 60% (Small & Medium) of the total project cost will be contributed by GoI up to a maximum of Rs. 40 lakh and the remaining project cost will be borne by MSMEs

programmes.name_local: MSME Innovative Scheme (Incubation, Design and IPR) under MSME Champions
programmes.name_en: MSME Innovative Scheme (Incubation, Design and IPR) under MSME Champions
programmes.funder: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME), Government of India
programmes.amount_note: Incubation: up to Rs 15 lakh per idea and up to Rs 1 crore for plant and machinery; design project up to Rs 40 lakh; seed capital equity up to Rs 1 crore at 80:20.

procedure_steps.detail: Identify an approved Host Institute on the MSME Innovative portal.
Submit the idea online through the Host Institute.
Screening committee evaluation and approval.
Funds released to the Host Institute for development of the idea.

eligibility.other_note: Individuals with an innovative idea and Udyam-registered MSMEs. The idea must be validated through an approved Host Institute. DPIIT recognition is not required.

programmes.source_snippet: Financial assistance up to Rs. 15 lakh per idea and up to Rs. 1.00 crore for relevant plant and machines will be provided.

programmes.name_en: MSME Competitive (LEAN) Scheme
programmes.funder: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME), Government of India
programmes.amount_note: Government pays 90% of the implementation cost of LEAN manufacturing consultancy (100% for women-owned and SC/ST-owned MSMEs and MSMEs in the ZED scheme or SFURTI clusters), plus a financial reward of INR 3.6 lakh on achieving the Basic level and higher rewards at Intermediate and Advanced levels.

eligibility.other_note: Udyam-registered MSMEs, individually or as a cluster. DPIIT recognition is not required.

programmes.name_en: Procurement and Marketing Support (PMS) Scheme
programmes.funder: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME), Government of India
programmes.amount_note: Reimbursement of stall rental, space rent and airfare for micro and small enterprises participating in domestic and international trade fairs and exhibitions, at 80-100% for special categories (SC/ST, women, North East, differently abled) and lower rates for the general category. Amounts are per event and capped by the scheme guidelines.
programmes.deadline_note: Support is event-linked; approved events and application windows are notified through the Ministry and its MSME Development and Facilitation Offices. Confirm the current operating guidelines, which have been revised under the consolidated MSME Champions umbrella.

eligibility.other_note: Udyam-registered micro and small enterprises. Support is per participating unit per event with an annual cap. DPIIT recognition is not required.

programmes.name_en: Raising and Accelerating MSME Performance (RAMP)
programmes.funder: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME), Government of India (World Bank-assisted)
programmes.amount_note: INR 6,062.45 crore World Bank-assisted programme. Money reaches enterprises indirectly through state-level Strategic Investment Plans and sub-schemes covering market access, digitalisation, greening, technology upgrade and women entrepreneurship. Individual amounts are set by each sub-scheme.
programmes.deadline_note: Delivered through state Strategic Investment Plans and periodic sub-scheme calls; check ramp.msme.gov.in and your state MSME department.

eligibility.other_note: Udyam-registered MSMEs. Specific eligibility varies by RAMP sub-scheme and by state.

programmes.source_snippet: A ₹6,062 crore central sector programme to supercharge market access, institutional strength, and green innovation for India's MSME sector.

programmes.name_en: MSME Sustainable (ZED) Certification Scheme
programmes.funder: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (Ministry of MSME), Government of India
programmes.amount_note: Subsidy on certification cost across three levels (Bronze, Silver, Gold), plus a joining reward, handholding support and testing/certification reimbursement, with additional subsidy for women-owned, SC/ST-owned, NER and aspirational-district units. The exact subsidy percentages and the joining reward amount are published in the scheme guidelines; the ZED guidelines page returned a robots error at the time of verification, so those figures are recorded as null rather than guessed. The official site reports 672,994 MSMEs registered and Rs 604.85 Cr of financial support provided to date.
programmes.deadline_note: Registration on the ZED portal is open continuously; no closing date is published.

procedure_steps.detail: Register the MSME free of cost on the ZED portal and take the ZED pledge.
Apply for Bronze, Silver or Gold certification and complete the assessment.
Claim the applicable subsidy, joining reward, handholding and testing/certification reimbursement.

eligibility.other_note: Open to manufacturing MSMEs with a valid Udyam Registration. The scheme encourages manufacturing with 'zero defect' and 'zero effect' on the environment. DPIIT startup recognition is not required; Udyam/MSME registration is. Additional incentives exist for women, SC/ST, NER and ZED-linked units.

programmes.source_snippet: Free ZED Certification For Women Owned MSMEs

programmes.name_local: SINE IIT Bombay incubation and seed support
programmes.name_en: SINE IIT Bombay incubation and seed support
programmes.funder: Society for Innovation and Entrepreneurship (SINE), IIT Bombay
programmes.amount_note: Incubation at IIT Bombay with access to DST NIDHI seed support, PRAYAS prototyping grants and, since 2025, an incubator-linked deep tech venture fund. Grant amounts follow the underlying DST instruments.
programmes.deadline_note: Incubation applications are accepted on a rolling basis; individual grant instruments follow DST NIDHI cycles.

eligibility.other_note: Technology startups willing to be physically incubated at IIT Bombay. IIT Bombay affiliation is not mandatory.

programmes.source_snippet: SINE at IIT Bombay supports tech startups with incubation, mentorship, funding, and resources to turn innovative ideas into successful ventures.

programmes.name_local: NABARD Rural Innovation Fund and Farm Sector Promotion Fund
programmes.name_en: NABARD Rural Innovation Fund and Farm Sector Promotion Fund
programmes.funder: National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD)
programmes.amount_note: Grant and soft-loan support for innovative, risky and unproven rural livelihood and farm-sector projects. Amounts are project-specific and sanctioned by NABARD regional offices. NABARD also runs NABVENTURES, a separate agri and food venture fund that takes equity.
programmes.deadline_note: Proposals are received round the year by NABARD regional offices; specific windows are notified regionally.

eligibility.other_note: Individuals, NGOs, cooperatives, producer organisations, agri-startups and rural institutions working on innovations in agriculture and rural livelihoods.

programmes.name_en: NIDHI Accelerator
programmes.funder: Department of Science and Technology (DST), Government of India
programmes.amount_note: NIDHI contribution up to Rs 40 lakh per accelerator programme (one cohort): up to Rs 30 lakh programme cost plus up to Rs 10 lakh demo-day awards. Applicants are TBIs/incubators.
programmes.deadline_note: Each NIDHI Accelerator announces its own cohort dates.

eligibility.other_note: Applicants are institutions: TBIs funded by DST or other central/state agencies, in existence at least 3 years, having incubated at least 20 startups.

programmes.source_snippet: The NIDHI-Accelerator contribution towards the overall Budget for running accelerators shall not exceed 40 Lakh/program of one cohort.

programmes.name_en: NIDHI Centre of Excellence (CoE)
programmes.funder: Department of Science and Technology (DST), Government of India
programmes.amount_note: Funds world-class incubation Centres of Excellence that host and scale deep-tech startups; support flows to the host institution rather than to startups directly.

eligibility.other_note: Startups engage via the CoE host institution.

programmes.source_snippet: Applications are invited for establishing NIDHI-CoE in institutions through call-for-proposals via Dept. of Science & Technology's e-PMS portal.

programmes.name_en: NIDHI Entrepreneur in Residence (EIR)
programmes.funder: Department of Science and Technology (DST), Government of India
programmes.amount_note: Fellowship of Rs 10,000 to Rs 30,000 per month for up to 12 months (max about Rs 3.6 lakh) plus TBI infrastructure and mentoring.
programmes.deadline_note: Host incubators announce EIR cohorts individually; there is no single national deadline.

eligibility.other_note: Indian citizens, typically graduates under 35, willing to work full time on a technology venture at a NIDHI-supported incubator. Cannot draw another salary or fellowship concurrently. DPIIT recognition is not required.

programmes.source_snippet: The NIDHI-EIR recipient is eligible to get financial support of up to INR 30,000/- monthly. The minimum financial support offered is INR 10,000/- monthly.

programmes.name_en: NIDHI-PRAYAS (Promoting and Accelerating Young and Aspiring Innovators and Startups)
programmes.funder: Department of Science and Technology (DST), Government of India, implemented with SINE, IIT Bombay
programmes.amount_note: PRAYAS 2.0: prototype funding up to Rs 20 lakh per innovator/startup; specialised DeepTech centres up to Rs 40 lakh.
programmes.deadline_note: Innovators apply through individual NIDHI-PRAYAS Centres hosted at selected Technology Business Incubators; each centre runs its own call. Centres themselves are selected through open calls published on the NIDHI-PRAYAS PMU website.

procedure_steps.detail: Read the NIDHI-PRAYAS guidelines.
Find a NIDHI-PRAYAS Centre (a selected TBI) near you from the official list.
Apply to that centre when its call is open; selected PRAYASEEs receive milestone-based prototype funding and Fab Lab access.

documents_required.doc: Prototype development proposal with milestones and budget
Proof of student / innovator status or entity registration

eligibility.other_note: Sector-agnostic. Beneficiaries are Students / Researchers / Innovators / Entrepreneurs / Startups; a registered company is not required at application stage. Emphasis on indigenously developed innovations aligned with the AtmaNirbhar Bharat Mission. DPIIT recognition is not stated as a prerequisite on the official DST page.

programmes.source_snippet: Support technology-based innovations with prototype funding of up to ₹20 Lakhs per innovator/startup.

programmes.name_en: NIDHI Seed Support System (NIDHI-SSS)
programmes.funder: Department of Science and Technology (DST), Government of India
programmes.amount_note: NIDHI Seed Support Program (NIDHI-SSP): max support up to INR 100 lakh per startup, via incubators that run periodic calls.
programmes.deadline_note: Applications go to the individual incubator holding an SSS corpus; each incubator runs its own selection.

eligibility.other_note: Startup must be physically incubated at the DST-supported incubator, incorporated in India with majority Indian shareholding, and have a technology-based product at or near market readiness. DPIIT recognition is commonly expected by host incubators.

programmes.source_snippet: The maximum support that will be given to a deserving startup is up to INR 100 lakh.

programmes.name_local: NIDHI Technology Business Incubator (TBI) and i-TBI
programmes.name_en: NIDHI Technology Business Incubator (TBI) and i-TBI
programmes.funder: Department of Science and Technology (DST), Government of India
programmes.amount_note: DST funds the incubator, not the startup. Startups get subsidised incubation space, labs, mentoring and access to NIDHI PRAYAS, EIR and SSS instruments through the host TBI. i-TBI supports new incubators in tier 2/3 cities and aspirational districts.

eligibility.other_note: Startups apply to individual TBIs. Host institution calls for new TBIs and i-TBIs are issued periodically by DST.

programmes.source_snippet: Applications are invited for establishing NIDHI-TBIs in institutions through call-for-proposals via Dept. of Science & Technology's e-PMS portal.

programmes.name_local: NSIC Raw Material Assistance and Single Point Registration Scheme
programmes.name_en: NSIC Raw Material Assistance and Single Point Registration Scheme
programmes.funder: National Small Industries Corporation (NSIC), Ministry of MSME
programmes.amount_note: Raw Material Assistance finances the purchase of raw material against a bank guarantee for up to 180 days. Single Point Registration gives free tender documents, exemption from Earnest Money Deposit and preference in government purchases. No cash grant.

eligibility.other_note: Udyam-registered micro and small enterprises in manufacturing or services. Units must have commenced commercial production; traders are excluded from Single Point Registration.

programmes.source_snippet: Raw Material Assistance Scheme aims at helping MSMEs by way of financing the purchase of Raw Material (Both indigenous & imported). ... credit support up to 180 days ... Security in the form of Bank Guarantee from Approved Banks.

programmes.name_en: Odisha Startup Hub (O-Hub) incubation
programmes.funder: Startup Odisha, MSME Department, Government of Odisha
programmes.amount_note: Subsidised incubation space, plug-and-play facilities, mentoring and investor connects at the Odisha Startup Hub in Bhubaneswar. No direct cash grant.

eligibility.other_note: Startup Odisha-recognised startups. DPIIT recognition is a prerequisite.

programmes.name_local: Startup Odisha product development and prototype grant
programmes.name_en: Startup Odisha product development and prototype grant
programmes.funder: Startup Odisha, MSME Department, Government of Odisha
programmes.amount_note: Monthly allowance of INR 20,000 (INR 22,000 where founders are women, transgender or from SC/ST/SEBC/PH categories), plus product development and marketing/publicity assistance, per the official Startup Odisha incentives page. Other ceilings are set in the current Odisha Startup Policy.
programmes.deadline_note: Applications are made on a rolling basis after obtaining Startup Odisha recognition.

procedure_steps.detail: Apply for Startup Odisha recognition on startupodisha.gov.in.
On recognition, apply for the specific incentive with supporting documents.
Departmental scrutiny and State Level Startup Committee approval.
Disbursement to the startup's bank account.

eligibility.other_note: DPIIT recognition is a prerequisite. Startup must additionally obtain Startup Odisha recognition and have its registered office or substantive operations in Odisha.

programmes.source_snippet: Monthly allowance of Rs.20,000 (Rs.22,000/-, if the startup Founder (s)/Co-Founder (s) are Women or transgender or from Social Categories such as SC/ST/SEBC/PH.

programmes.name_en: Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC)
programmes.funder: ONDC (Section 8 company promoted by DPIIT)
programmes.amount_note: No grant to startups. An open protocol network letting small sellers and startups plug into digital commerce through network participant apps; ONDC has periodically run subsidy and incentive programmes for network participants.

eligibility.other_note: Open to sellers, logistics providers and technology startups willing to onboard as Network Participants under the ONDC protocol.

programmes.source_snippet: Onboard once and reach customers across the network. ... Lower participation costs; Cataloguing, logistics and onboarding support available

programmes.name_local: Startup Punjab incentives under the Punjab Industrial and Business Development Policy
programmes.name_en: Startup Punjab incentives under the Punjab Industrial and Business Development Policy
programmes.funder: Department of Industries and Commerce, Government of Punjab (Invest Punjab)
programmes.amount_note: Incentives for recognised startups including lease rental subsidy at approved incubators, reimbursement of patent and quality certification costs, and marketing and event participation support. Ceilings are set in the Punjab Industrial and Business Development Policy.

eligibility.other_note: DPIIT recognition is a prerequisite. Startup must be registered in Punjab and recognised under the state startup framework.

programmes.name_en: Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Schemes
programmes.funder: Various line ministries (DPIIT, MeitY, Ministry of Textiles, Department of Pharmaceuticals, MNRE and others)
programmes.amount_note: Incentive paid as a percentage (typically 4-6%, higher in some sectors) of incremental sales of eligible goods manufactured in India over a base year, for five years. Minimum investment and turnover thresholds are high, so PLI is generally reachable only by scaled manufacturing companies rather than early-stage startups.
