programmes.deadline_note: PLI is implemented across 14 sectors, each run by its own ministry with its own application windows (for example the White Goods PLI Round 4 window ran until 10 November 2025). Check the administering ministry for the specific sector.

eligibility.other_note: Companies registered in India that commit to minimum incremental investment and incremental sales thresholds set per sector. Not suited to pre-revenue startups. DPIIT recognition is not required.

programmes.source_snippet: the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) schemes have been implemented across 14 key sectors ... by incentivizing incremental production and sales

programmes.name_en: Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana (PMMY)
programmes.funder: Micro Units Development and Refinance Agency (MUDRA) Ltd / Department of Financial Services
programmes.amount_note: Collateral-free loans to non-farm micro enterprises in four categories: Shishu up to INR 50,000, Kishore above INR 50,000 up to INR 5 lakh, Tarun above INR 5 lakh up to INR 10 lakh, and Tarun Plus above INR 10 lakh up to INR 20 lakh for borrowers who have repaid an earlier Tarun loan.

procedure_steps.detail: Apply at any bank, RRB, small finance bank, NBFC or MFI, or online via the Jan Samarth portal.
Submit the business plan and KYC; no collateral is required.
Lender sanctions and disburses; a MUDRA card may be issued for working capital.

documents_required.doc: Proof of business address and identity
Quotations for machinery or equipment where applicable

eligibility.other_note: Indian citizens running or setting up a non-farm income-generating micro enterprise in manufacturing, trading, services or allied agriculture, with credit need up to INR 20 lakh. DPIIT recognition is not required.

programmes.source_snippet: Collateral-free loans up to Rs 20 lakh for activities covering manufacturing, trading, services & allied agricultural activities. Tarun Plus category extends loans above Rs 10 lakh and up to Rs 20 lakh to borrowers who have successfully repaid previous loans under the Tarun category.

programmes.name_en: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP)
programmes.funder: Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC), Ministry of MSME
programmes.amount_note: Credit-linked capital subsidy on a bank loan. Project cost ceiling INR 50 lakh for manufacturing and INR 20 lakh for service units. Margin money subsidy of 15-25% in urban/rural areas for general category and 25-35% for special categories (SC/ST/OBC/minorities/women/ex-servicemen/differently abled/North East/hill and border areas).
programmes.deadline_note: Fresh application submission under PMEGP is presently unavailable; it will be enabled once the competent authority approves continuation of the Scheme with revised guidelines.
programmes.reopen_note: Facility will be enabled upon approval for continuation of the scheme with revised guidelines; check the PMEGP portal for updates.

procedure_steps.detail: Register and file the online application on the PMEGP e-portal.
District Level Task Force Committee interview and sponsorship to a bank.
Bank sanctions and disburses the loan; margin money subsidy is held in a Term Deposit Receipt for three years.
Complete EDP training; the subsidy is adjusted after the lock-in period.

documents_required.doc: Caste or special category certificate where claimed
Educational qualification certificate for projects above the specified cost

eligibility.other_note: For NEW units only; existing units and units already availing a government subsidy are ineligible. Applicants must be at least 18 years old; a minimum Class VIII pass is required for manufacturing projects above INR 10 lakh and service projects above INR 5 lakh. Own contribution of 10% (5% for special categories) required. DPIIT recognition is not required.

programmes.source_snippet: Fresh application submission under PMEGP is presently unavailable. The facility will be enabled upon approval for continuation of the Scheme with the revised guidelines by the competent authority.

programmes.name_en: iStart Rajasthan Seed Funding
programmes.funder: Department of Information Technology and Communication, Government of Rajasthan
programmes.amount_note: Rajasthan Startup Policy 2022 (iStart): Ideation grant of INR 2,40,000 for pre-seed startups (plus INR 60,000 extra if more than 50% equity is held by women founders); Viability grant for seed-stage startups of INR 10 lakh (non-QRate) rising to INR 20/30/40 lakh for Bronze QRate bands and INR 60 lakh for Silver and above.

eligibility.other_note: Startup must be registered on iStart Rajasthan with stage Idea or Prototype and hold a QRate rating. A cooling period of about 6 months applies between Seed Fund, Marketing Assistance and Techno Fund disbursements.

programmes.source_snippet: Ideation grant For Pre Seed Stage Startups: INR 2,40,000. Startups which have more than 50% equity with women founders will be provided an additional INR 60,000.

programmes.name_en: iStart Rajasthan Sustenance Allowance
programmes.funder: Department of Information Technology and Communication, Government of Rajasthan
programmes.amount_note: Monthly sustenance allowance paid to founders of idea or prototype stage startups for a fixed period, with higher rates for women, SC/ST and differently abled founders. Rates are set in the current Rajasthan Startup Policy notification.

procedure_steps.detail: Register the startup on the iStart Rajasthan portal and obtain a QRate rating.
Apply for the sustenance allowance with the startup at Idea or Prototype stage.
Evaluation and approval by the state committee.
Monthly disbursement for the approved period.

eligibility.other_note: Startup must be registered on iStart Rajasthan and its stage must be Idea or Prototype. If Seed Fund, Marketing Assistance or Techno Fund has already been disbursed, the applicant must wait approximately 6 months before applying for another of these instruments. DPIIT recognition is not mandatory for iStart registration.

programmes.source_snippet: Sustenance Allowance/ Seed Funding: Startup stage must be Idea/Prototype

programmes.name_local: iStart Rajasthan Techno Fund and Marketing Assistance
programmes.name_en: iStart Rajasthan Techno Fund and Marketing Assistance
programmes.funder: Department of Information Technology and Communication, Government of Rajasthan
programmes.amount_note: Techno Fund supports startups at the early traction and scaling stage; Marketing Assistance supports startups at the MVP stage with market entry and promotion costs. Ceilings are set in the current policy.

eligibility.other_note: Techno Fund requires a QRate-rated startup at Early Traction/Scaling stage; Marketing Assistance requires the startup to be at MVP stage. A cooling period of about 6 months applies between these instruments.

programmes.source_snippet: Techno Fund: Startup must be Qrate, Startup stage must be Early Traction Scaling

programmes.name_local: RKVY Innovation and Agri-entrepreneurship Development Programme (RKVY-RAFTAAR)
programmes.name_en: RKVY Innovation and Agri-entrepreneurship Development Programme (RKVY-RAFTAAR)
programmes.funder: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
programmes.amount_note: Idea/pre-seed stage grant of up to INR 5 lakh and seed stage grant of up to INR 25 lakh, released in tranches through an RKVY-RAFTAAR Agribusiness Incubator after a two-month incubation programme.
programmes.deadline_note: Applications are made to an RKVY-RAFTAAR Agribusiness Incubator (for example at NAARM Hyderabad, CIIE at IIM Ahmedabad, or IARI) when it announces a cohort. Confirm with the incubator whether the current RKVY cycle is funding startups.

procedure_steps.detail: Choose an RKVY-RAFTAAR Agribusiness Incubator and apply during its cohort call.
Screening and selection by the incubator's committee.
Complete the two-month agribusiness incubation programme.
Grant released in tranches against milestones, with a beneficiary contribution.

eligibility.other_note: Indian agri-startups and agripreneurs. Seed-stage applicants need a registered entity with a working prototype and early revenue; idea-stage applicants may be individuals. Beneficiary contribution of about 10% is expected. DPIIT recognition is not mandatory.

programmes.source_snippet: financial support upto Rs. 5.00 lakh is provided at the idea/pre seed stage and upto Rs. 25 lakh at the seed stage ... 90% grant and 10% contribution from the incubatee

programmes.name_en: Section 80-IAC Income Tax Exemption (three-year tax holiday for DPIIT-recognised startups)
programmes.funder: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) / Central Board of Direct Taxes, Government of India
programmes.amount_note: 100% deduction of profits and gains for 3 consecutive financial years, chosen by the startup out of its first ten years since incorporation. The value depends entirely on the startup's taxable profits, so no cash cap is published.
programmes.deadline_note: Applications are accepted on a rolling basis on the Startup India portal and are cleared in batches by the Inter-Ministerial Board. No fixed annual cut-off is published on the official page.

procedure_steps.detail: Obtain DPIIT Startup Recognition first.
Submit Form 80-IAC on the Startup India portal.
Inter-Ministerial Board evaluates; track outcome via the application status page.

documents_required.doc: Annual accounts and income tax returns for the last three financial years
Pitch deck / video link describing the innovation

eligibility.other_note: The entity should be a recognised Startup; only a Private Limited Company or a Limited Liability Partnership is eligible under Section 80-IAC (a registered partnership firm or cooperative society recognised by DPIIT is not); and the Startup should have been incorporated after 1st April, 2016. DPIIT recognition is a hard prerequisite: the startup must hold a DPIIT Certificate of Recognition obtained through the National Single Window System (nsws.gov.in) before it can apply. Per the official recognition page the entity must be a Private Limited Company, Registered Partnership Firm, LLP or Cooperative Society, with turnover under INR 200 crore (INR 300 crore for DeepTech) in any previous financial year, and is treated as a startup for up to 10 years (20 years for DeepTech) from incorporation.

programmes.source_snippet: Post getting recognition a Startup may apply for Tax exemption under section 80 IAC of the Income Tax Act. Post getting clearance for Tax exemption, the Startup can avail tax holiday for 3 consecutive financial years out of its first ten years since incorporation. ... Only Private limited or a Limited Liability Partnership is eligible for Tax exemption under Section 80IAC. The Startup should have been incorporated after 1st April, 2016.

programmes.name_local: SFURTI - Scheme of Fund for Regeneration of Traditional Industries
programmes.name_en: SFURTI - Scheme of Fund for Regeneration of Traditional Industries
programmes.funder: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME), Government of India
programmes.amount_note: Project outlay per cluster: heritage cluster (1000-2500 artisans) up to INR 8 crore, major cluster (500-1000 artisans) up to INR 3 crore, mini cluster (up to 500 artisans) up to INR 1.5 crore. Soft interventions up to INR 25 lakh (100% scheme funding); hard interventions 75% scheme funding.

eligibility.other_note: Applications are made by Implementing Agencies (NGOs, central or state government institutions, semi-government institutions, field functionaries, Panchayati Raj institutions) on behalf of artisan clusters in traditional industries such as khadi, coir and village industries.

programmes.source_snippet: Heritage cluster (1000-2500 artisans): Rs 8 crore; Major cluster (500-1000 artisans): Rs 3 crore; Mini cluster (Up to 500 artisans): Rs 1.5 crore.

programmes.name_local: स्टार्टअप्स के लिए फंड ऑफ फंड्स
programmes.name_en: Fund of Funds for Startups (FFS), operated by SIDBI
programmes.funder: Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI), on behalf of DPIIT, Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India
programmes.amount_note: No direct grant: the Fund of Funds for Startups invests via SEBI-registered Alternative Investment Funds from an approved corpus of INR 10,000 crore, and a Startup India Fund of Funds 2.0 with a corpus of INR 10,000 crore has been announced. Startups receive money from the AIFs, not from SIDBI directly.
programmes.deadline_note: AIF managers approach SIDBI Venture Capital for commitments; there is no application route for individual startups.

procedure_steps.detail: Startups: identify and pitch to Alternative Investment Funds that have received an FFS commitment from SIDBI.
Fund managers: apply to SIDBI Venture Capital Ltd for a commitment from the Fund of Funds for Startups.

documents_required.doc: For AIFs: SEBI AIF registration and fund documents

eligibility.other_note: Indirect instrument. The startup-facing eligibility condition is that the investee must qualify as a startup under the DPIIT definition for the AIF's FFS-attributable investment to count, so DPIIT recognition is effectively required for the FFS-linked portion. Terms are set by the AIF, not by SIDBI or DPIIT.

programmes.source_snippet: It has approved corpus of Rs 10,000 crore for contribution to various Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs) registered with SEBI.

programmes.name_en: Stand-Up India Scheme
programmes.funder: Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance / SIDBI
programmes.amount_note: Composite loan (term loan plus working capital) between INR 10 lakh and INR 1 crore for setting up a greenfield enterprise, covering up to 85% of project cost. Margin money requirement is 15% of project cost, which may be met in convergence with eligible central or state schemes; the borrower must bring at least 10%.
programmes.deadline_note: Rolling via bank branches. The 2025 PIB note describes the scheme in the past tense and does not state a validity period or extension; confirm current availability with a bank branch or standupmitra.in.

procedure_steps.detail: Register on the Stand-Up India portal (standupmitra.in) and select handholding support if needed.
The application is routed to a scheduled commercial bank branch.
Bank appraises the greenfield project and sanctions the composite loan.
Repayment over up to 7 years with a moratorium of up to 18 months.

documents_required.doc: Proof of SC/ST status or gender
Proof that the enterprise is greenfield
Quotations and lease or ownership documents for premises

eligibility.other_note: Borrower must be SC/ST and/or a woman entrepreneur above 18 years of age. The enterprise must be GREENFIELD - the borrower's first venture in manufacturing, services, trading or allied agricultural activities. For non-individual entities, at least 51% shareholding and controlling stake must be held by an SC/ST and/or woman entrepreneur. Borrower must not be in default to any bank or financial institution.

programmes.source_snippet: The Scheme provided loans of value between Rs. 10 lakh and Rs.1 Crore ... to at least one SC or ST borrower and one woman borrower per Bank branch for setting up a greenfield enterprise

programmes.name_en: Abolition of Angel Tax (Section 56(2)(viib))
programmes.funder: Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT), Ministry of Finance
programmes.amount_note: No cash. Union Budget 2024-25 abolished Section 56(2)(viib) for all classes of investors with effect from assessment year 2025-26, removing the angel tax on share premium above fair market value. This replaces the earlier DPIIT exemption process under Form 2.

procedure_steps.detail: No application needed — this is paid automatically to everyone who qualifies. Check that the authority holds your current address and bank details; a missing detail is the usual reason an automatic payment does not arrive.

eligibility.other_note: Applies to all companies from AY 2025-26; DPIIT recognition is no longer needed to escape angel tax, though it remains needed for 80-IAC and other benefits.

programmes.source_snippet: The Finance Act (No. 2) 2024 removed Section 56 (2) (viib) (angel tax provisions) from the Income Tax Act effective 1st April 2025.

programmes.name_en: Startup India Investor Connect
programmes.funder: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT)
programmes.amount_note: No direct money. A matchmaking platform launched in 2023 that connects DPIIT-recognised startups with registered angel investors, VC funds and family offices, and hosts curated pitching sessions.

eligibility.other_note: DPIIT recognition is a prerequisite.

programmes.source_snippet: Startup India Investor Connect is a platform that connects startups with investors to facilitate investment opportunities.

programmes.name_local: Public procurement relaxations for startups (GeM Startup Runway)
programmes.name_en: Public procurement relaxations for startups (GeM Startup Runway)
programmes.funder: Government e-Marketplace (GeM), Ministry of Commerce and Industry
programmes.amount_note: No grant. DPIIT-recognised startups are exempted from prior turnover and prior experience requirements and from Earnest Money Deposit in central government tenders, and can sell innovative products on the GeM Startup Runway.

procedure_steps.detail: No application needed — this is paid automatically to everyone who qualifies. Check that the authority holds your current address and bank details; a missing detail is the usual reason an automatic payment does not arrive.

eligibility.other_note: DPIIT recognition is a prerequisite. Quality and technical specifications of the tender must still be met.

programmes.source_snippet: Startups are exempted from otherwise stringent selection criteria such as Prior Experience, Prior Turnover and Earnest Money Deposits

programmes.name_en: Startup India Seed Fund Scheme (SISFS)
programmes.funder: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India
programmes.amount_note: Two instruments, each available once per startup. (1) Up to Rs. 20 Lakhs as grant for validation of Proof of Concept, prototype development or product trials, disbursed in milestone-based instalments. (2) Up to Rs. 50 Lakhs of investment for market entry, commercialization or scaling up, through convertible debentures or debt or debt-linked instruments, at a rate of interest of not more than the prevailing repo rate. Money is not paid by DPIIT directly: it is disbursed through the selected incubator. Total scheme outlay is INR 945 crore.
programmes.deadline_note: The scheme originally ran year-round Calls for Applications. As of 14 August 2026 the SISFS portal carries a banner reading 'Final Notice (Extended): Last date for startups to apply under SISFS - 31 May 2026 | Incubators to complete 100% startup selection by - 30 June 2026.' That startup application deadline has passed, so the scheme is not accepting new startup applications at the time of verification. No successor call had been announced on the official site.

procedure_steps.detail: Obtain DPIIT Startup Recognition via the National Single Window System.
Register on the SISFS portal and apply to up to three eligible incubators simultaneously, choosing grant and/or debt instrument.
Incubator's Incubator Seed Management Committee (ISMC) evaluates and selects startups.
Sign the agreement with the incubator; funds released against agreed milestones.

documents_required.doc: Shareholding pattern showing at least 51% Indian promoter shareholding
documents_required.note: Per Companies Act 2013 and SEBI (ICDR) Regulations 2018

eligibility.other_note: A startup, recognized by DPIIT, incorporated not more than 2 years ago at the time of application. Must use technology in its core product/service, business model, distribution model or methodology. Must not have received more than Rs 10 lakh of monetary support under any other Central or State Government scheme (prize money, subsidised workspace, founder allowance, lab or prototyping access excluded). Shareholding by Indian promoters must be at least 51% at the time of application. Preference for social impact, waste management, water management, financial inclusion, education, agriculture, food processing, biotechnology, healthcare, energy, mobility, defence, space, railways, oil and gas, textiles. No mandatory physical incubation. DPIIT recognition is a hard prerequisite: the startup must hold a DPIIT Certificate of Recognition obtained through the National Single Window System (nsws.gov.in) before it can apply. Per the official recognition page the entity must be a Private Limited Company, Registered Partnership Firm, LLP or Cooperative Society, with turnover under INR 200 crore (INR 300 crore for DeepTech) in any previous financial year, and is treated as a startup for up to 10 years (20 years for DeepTech) from incorporation.

programmes.source_snippet: An online call for applications is hosted on an ongoing basis on the Startup India portal will be opened soon. ... Up to Rs. 20 Lakhs as grant ... Up to Rs. 50 Lakhs of investment ... incorporated not more than 2 years ago
programmes.reopen_note: The official FAQ says an online call for applications will be opened soon on the Startup India portal; no date announced.

programmes.name_en: Technology Development Board (TDB) financial assistance for commercialisation of indigenous technology
programmes.funder: Technology Development Board (TDB), Department of Science & Technology, Government of India
programmes.amount_note: Three modes. Loan: soft loan at 5% simple interest per annum, covering 50% of the un-incurred project cost. Equity: up to 25% of the approved project cost, provided such investment does not exceed the capital paid up by the promoters. Grant: only in exceptional cases of national interest. TDB does not publish a fixed per-project ceiling; the amount follows the approved project cost.
programmes.deadline_note: TDB Core Funding runs an open Call for Proposal via the e-TechCom portal. Separate time-bound calls run alongside it, e.g. the India-Finland Joint Innovation Call 2026 and the RDI Fund call (RDIF 2026), listed under 'Active Calls' on the TDB homepage.

procedure_steps.detail: Review the TDB modes of funding and project funding guidelines.
Register your company on the TDB e-TechCom portal and submit the proposal.
Technical and financial appraisal, followed by the Board's decision and signing of an agreement.

documents_required.doc: Detailed project report with project cost breakdown
Evidence of indigenous technology or technology transfer agreement
Audited financial statements of the industrial concern
Promoters' contribution / means of finance statement

eligibility.other_note: Open to Indian industrial concerns and other agencies attempting development and commercial application of indigenous technology, or adapting imported technology to wider domestic applications. Not limited to startups. DPIIT recognition is not stated as a prerequisite for TDB core funding.

programmes.source_snippet: The financial assistance to the industrial concerns is provided a soft loan at 5% simple interest per annum. The financial assistance is 50 % of the un incurred project cost. ... TDB contributes by way of equity capital in an industrial concern on its commencement start-up and/or growth stages. It is up to 25 % of the approved project cost, provided such investment does not exceed the capital paid up by the promoters.

programmes.funder: Technology Development Board, Department of Science and Technology

Approval by the Board and execution of a loan agreement.
Disbursement in tranches against project milestones.

Audited financials for the last three years
Means of finance and promoter contribution

programmes.source_snippet: Loan: Up to 50% of the project cost at 5% simple annual interest in general.

programmes.source_snippet: The campaign aims to reach out to every member of every household to encourage them to think of themselves as problem solvers

Screening, regional pitching rounds and a final jury.
Grant disbursed in tranches with an accompanying acceleration programme.

programmes.amount_note: Per the Startup India Schemes Playbook (June 2026) summarising the SBIRI guidelines: 100% BIRAC grant-in-aid for project cost up to INR 50 lakh; above that, INR 50 lakh plus 70% of the cost over INR 50 lakh; the applicant bears the rest. No fixed upper cap is stated on the BIRAC page.
programmes.deadline_note: Two regular calls a year: 1 April to 15 May and 1 September to 15 October (current window ends 15 October 2026 if the standing schedule applies; BIRAC may also announce extra calls).

procedure_steps.detail: Read the SBIRI scheme document and prepare the proposal in the prescribed proforma.
Submit during an open call window.

eligibility.other_note: Company (Companies Act 2013) or LLP, or a joint venture with a university/institute; at least 51% shares held by Indian citizens (not PIO/OCI) or at least half of LLP partners Indian citizens; adequate in-house facility or incubated at a recognised incubator. Early-stage pre-proof-of-concept biotech R&D.

programmes.source_snippet: Minimum 51% of the shares of the Company should be held by Indian Citizens holding Indian passport

programmes.name_local: AgriSURE Fund (Agri Fund for Start-ups and Rural Enterprises)
programmes.name_en: AgriSURE Fund (Agri Fund for Start-ups and Rural Enterprises)
programmes.funder: NABVENTURES Ltd (sponsored by NABARD and Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare)
programmes.amount_note: Direct Scheme (INR 300 crore) invests up to INR 25 crore in one DPIIT-recognised start-up in equity or CCPS; FoF Scheme (INR 450 crore) invests in agri/rural AIFs. Total corpus INR 750 crore. No fee is charged for seeking assistance.
programmes.deadline_note: Start-ups may reach out to the Investment Manager at any time.

procedure_steps.detail: Email the Investment Manager (agrisure@nabard.org) with your proposal.

eligibility.other_note: DPIIT-recognised start-ups incorporated in India working in agriculture and rural development (agritech, food processing, animal husbandry, fisheries, supply chain, farm mechanisation, biotechnology, waste management, renewable energy, FPO support, climate). Merely qualifying does not guarantee investment.

programmes.source_snippet: The Scheme will make investment of upto a maximum of ₹25 crore in one Start-up, subject to AIF Regulations.

programmes.name_en: iDEX (Innovations for Defence Excellence)
programmes.funder: Defence Innovation Organisation, Department of Defence Production, Ministry of Defence
programmes.amount_note: Selected applicants are funded up to INR 1.5 crore (equity or other relevant structures), disbursed in tranches against milestones, plus access to accelerators and defence testing facilities. The iDEX FAQ confirms winners under DISC and Open Challenges can receive grants up to INR 1.5 crore subject to approval of the Product Development Budget.
programmes.deadline_note: Apply against open iDEX challenges; each challenge sets its own window.

procedure_steps.detail: Provide point-of-contact, entity details and the proposal against an iDEX challenge problem statement.
Screening by a high-powered committee of defence and technology experts.
Funding in tranches against milestones.

eligibility.other_note: DPIIT-recognised startups, Indian MSME companies (Companies Act) and individual innovators; per the iDEX FAQ a startup needs majority Indian stake. Apply against iDEX challenge problem statements; funds are for R&D, prototyping, pilot implementation and market assessment.

programmes.source_snippet: The selected applications will be funded up to ₹1.5 crores in the form of equity/other relevant structures.

programmes.name_local: STPI Next Generation Incubation Scheme (NGIS) Seed Funding
programmes.name_en: STPI Next Generation Incubation Scheme (NGIS) Seed Funding
programmes.funder: Software Technology Parks of India (STPI), Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
programmes.amount_note: Seed/risk funding of up to INR 25 lakh for promising tech startups, plus incubation infrastructure, labs, mentoring, startup-connect, marketing support and internship grants, delivered from 12 STPI centres.
programmes.deadline_note: Open through NGIS challenges and calls; dates are not published on the portal page.

procedure_steps.detail: Apply through the NGIS programme page or an All India Start-up Challenge.

eligibility.other_note: Technology startups building software products. NGIS runs from 12 STPI centres: Agartala, Bhilai, Bhopal, Bhubaneswar, Dehradun, Guwahati, Jaipur, Lucknow, Prayagraj, Mohali, Patna and Vijayawada. Intake is through All India Start-up Challenges/Hackathons.

programmes.source_snippet: Avail upto Rs.25 Lakh of Seed/Risk Funding for promising startups.

programmes.name_local: PM Formalisation of Micro Food Processing Enterprises (PMFME) Scheme
programmes.name_en: PM Formalisation of Micro Food Processing Enterprises (PMFME) Scheme
programmes.funder: Ministry of Food Processing Industries (MoFPI), Government of India
programmes.amount_note: Credit-linked capital subsidy of 35% of eligible project cost, up to INR 10 lakh per unit (individuals, proprietorships, partnerships, FPOs, NGOs, cooperatives, SHGs, Pvt Ltd companies). Groups building common infrastructure get 35% up to INR 3 crore; SHG members get seed capital of INR 40,000 each (up to INR 4 lakh per SHG); 50% grant for group branding and marketing.
programmes.deadline_note: Applications are taken on the PMFME portal; no closing date is published.

procedure_steps.detail: Register and apply on the PMFME portal; apply for a bank loan through the portal.

eligibility.other_note: Existing and new micro food processing units, FPOs, SHGs and cooperatives, including those under the One District One Product approach. The subsidy is credit-linked, so a bank loan is needed.

programmes.source_snippet: Individuals / Proprietorship / Partnership/ FPOs/ NGOs/ Cooperatives/ SHGs/ Pvt. Ltd. Co. would be provided credit-linked capital subsidy @35% of the eligible project cost - maximum of Rs. 10.0 lakhs per unit for upgradation or setting up of new units.

programmes.name_local: MeitY Design Linked Incentive (DLI) Scheme for Semiconductor Design
programmes.name_en: MeitY Design Linked Incentive (DLI) Scheme for Semiconductor Design
programmes.funder: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY); nodal agency C-DAC
programmes.amount_note: Product Design Linked Incentive: reimbursement of up to 50% of eligible expenditure, capped at INR 15 crore per application. Deployment Linked Incentive: 6% to 4% of net sales turnover over 5 years, capped at INR 30 crore per application. Design infrastructure support (EDA tool grid, IP cores, MPW prototyping, post-silicon validation) for startups and MSMEs.
programmes.deadline_note: Application window is not stated on the FAQ page; check the DLI portal.

procedure_steps.detail: Pay the INR 10,000 registration fee and submit the online application with applicant details and a Detailed Project Report on the DLI portal.
C-DAC examines the application and issues an approval letter with milestones.
Reimbursement is paid against milestones.

eligibility.other_note: Domestic companies (more than 50% owned by resident Indian citizens), DPIIT-recognised startups and MSMEs working on semiconductor design for ICs, chipsets, SoCs, systems and IP cores. Online application with a registration fee of INR 10,000 and a Detailed Project Report.

programmes.source_snippet: Reimbursement of up to 50% of the eligible expenditure subject to a ceiling of ₹15 Crore per application
